title: Running Your Own DNS Resolver Requires a Clear Operating Plan

cover.subtitle: Choose the architecture. Test privately. Plan recovery.
cover.visual: A local resolver sits inside a private network beside operation and recovery cards.

sections.name: 01-architecture
sections.heading: Recursion and forwarding create different operating responsibilities
sections.scene: Three distinct diagrams show local recursion toward authoritative servers, forwarding toward a selected resolver, and a separate dynamic DNS address update.
sections.alt: Recursion, forwarding, and dynamic DNS perform different tasks.

sections.name: 02-pilot
sections.heading: A private pilot starts with supported installation and limited access
sections.scene: One test device connects to a local resolver behind a private access boundary and configuration checklist.
sections.alt: A private pilot limits listener and client access.

sections.name: 03-verification
sections.heading: Validation and privacy settings need separate verification
sections.scene: Two independent check cards show DNSSEC authenticity and authenticated transport encryption beside a query log setting.
sections.alt: DNSSEC validation and transport encryption need separate checks.

sections.name: 04-operation
sections.heading: A network rollout needs availability and abuse controls
sections.scene: A small private network uses a maintained resolver with reboot recovery, update, and access review checklist. No public inbound port appears.
sections.alt: A network resolver requires maintenance and limited access.
